newsitem.title: GREECE: National Bank/Greece to cut depo, loan rates Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: National Bank/Greece to cut depo, loan rates Jan 7.

text.p: The National Bank of Greece, the country's largest commercial bank, will cut its deposit rates by 50 basis points and its lending rates by 25 to 125 basis points effective January 7, a high-level bank source told Reuters.

"After taking into consideration the prevailing market conditions, the positive economic climate and in the context of its greater strategy, the National Bank of Greece decided to proceed with sizeable interest rate cuts effective January 7," the high-level bank source said.
The high-level source also cited the recent interest rate cuts on government securities by the finance ministry as an additional reason for cutting its deposit and lending rates.
The base deposit rate and the current deposit account will be cut by 50 basis points to 10.25 percent and 8.75 percent respectively, he said.
The working capital lending rate will be slashed 75 basis points to 16.75 percent and the adjustable rate for fixed asset loans by 125 basis points to 15 percent, the source said.
The fixed rate loans for fixed assets will be reduced to 13.75 percent from 14 percent, the adjustable mortgage rate will be decreased by 50 basis points to 14.75 percent, he said.

Consumer loan rates will be cut 100 basis points to 22.75 percent, special consumer loans by 50 basis points to 19.5 percent, personal loan rates by 75 basis points to 24 percent, credit card rates by 25 basis points to 26 percent from January 7, he said.
